title: Part 5 — Node, Express & MySQL
tagline: An Express 5 server, MySQL on your machine, and code split into MVC.
intro: This part moves to the server: take requests, read and write a database, send results back. It is still JavaScript, run by part 1's Node.
MySQL is the main database. F8's Node video uses MongoDB; learn the moves from it, then apply them to MySQL with the steps here.

blocks.caption: From a server that says hello to an API reading real data from MySQL.

items.label: First Express server
items.detail: Ten lines that take a request and answer with text or JSON
explain: app.get('/api/courses', handler) means: on a GET to /api/courses, run handler. res.json() answers with JSON.
node --watch server.js restarts the server on every save, replacing the video's nodemon.

items.label: Routes & MVC
items.detail: Split code: routes take paths, controllers do the work, models talk to the database
explain: A route only ties a path to a function. The controller reads the request, calls the model and picks the status. The model is the only place with SQL.
F8's video adds Handlebars views to render HTML on the server. Part 6 drops the views and returns JSON to React instead.

items.label: Install MySQL
items.detail: A database server on your machine, with a visual tool for browsing tables
explain: Windows installs MySQL inside Ubuntu (WSL) with apt; macOS installs mysql@8.4 with Homebrew. Both create a separate user for code, never root.
DBeaver or MySQL Workbench let you browse tables, edit rows and run SQL with the mouse, handy while learning.

items.label: SQL
items.detail: Create tables, insert, read, update and delete rows, and join tables
explain: Each table has a primary key id. A foreign key links tables: products.category_id points at categories.id, so each product has a category.
JOIN combines two tables by key: product names with their category names in a single SELECT.

items.label: Connect Express to MySQL
items.detail: The mysql2 library runs SQL from code; the password lives in a .env file
explain: Pass values through ? instead of joining strings: pool.query('… WHERE id = ?', [id]). Joining strings opens the door to SQL injection.
node --env-file=.env loads environment variables from the file, replacing the dotenv library. .env always goes in .gitignore.

items.label: Sessions & JWT
items.detail: Two ways a server remembers who is signed in; understand here, build in part 6
explain: Sessions: the server keeps the signed-in list and the browser holds a cookie with the session id. JWT: the server signs a token the client sends with each request.
F8's three videos on cookies, CORS and JWT explain the mechanics; each runs 40–90 minutes, so watch in pieces and take notes.

Not using WSL: download the MySQL Community Server 8.4 LTS MSI from dev.mysql.com; the bundled MySQL Configurator asks for a root password. The XAMPP in the SERN video installs MariaDB, close to MySQL but not it.

JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id;

sections.title: Connect Express to MySQL
sections.summary: An API reading real products from the shop database.

items: In shop-api, install mysql2: npm install mysql2.
Create a .env with the connection details, and add .env and node_modules to .gitignore.
Create config/db.js with one shared connection pool.
Add two product routes to server.js, or use the MVC section's route and controller.
Run the server with --env-file and open localhost:3000/api/products: the product list from MySQL means done.

blocks.caption: config/db.js: one pool for the whole app.
Add to server.js: read all and read by id, with values passed through ?.
code: const [rows] = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = ?', [req.params.id]);
if (rows.length === 0) return res.status(404).json({ message: 'Không tìm thấy' });

blocks.caption: Run with the .env variables and restart on save.

body: Never join user input into an SQL string, like 'WHERE id = ' + req.params.id. Always use ? with an array of values.

sections.title: Sequelize, as in the SERN course
sections.summary: JavaScript instead of SQL; the SERN course works this way from lesson #20.

items: An ORM like Sequelize turns tables into classes: User.findAll() instead of SELECT * FROM users.
A migration is a file describing a table change; running db:migrate gives every machine the same schema.
Learn plain SQL first: when Sequelize fails, the SQL it prints is what you need to read.

blocks.caption: Install Sequelize and its CLI, generate a User model and migrate. Update config/config.json from your .env first.
